title: Rustify batcher adapter and introduce KV-cache checkpoint protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The current monolithic C++ batcher adapter mixes IO, admission logic and KV-cache bookkeeping. This causes hard-to-debug memory-safety hotspots, slow iterations on scheduler changes, and ambiguous ownership for KV checkpointing. Goal: incrementally replace the hotpath adapter with a thin Rust shim that exposes a stable stage-fanout interface and add an explicit KV-cache checkpoint/rehydration protocol so shards can be reconciled without full-stop restarts. Constraints: keep end-to-end latency SLOs, avoid any customer-visible token losses during rollout, and ship with feature flags to allow quick rollback. Approach: 1) Implement Rust adapter that mirrors current adapter API but compiles to a C ABI; 2) Add a versioned KV checkpoint manifest format (JSON-lines with shard epoch, last_seq, tombstones); 3) Introduce a lightweight reconciler loop in the scheduler to apply checkpoints during warmup; 4) Add test harnesses and fuzzing for the new checkpoint parsing and for concurrent reads during warmup. Non-goals: not reworking the model of admission credits in this ticket — that will follow in a separate pass.
acceptance_criteria: New Rust adapter deployed behind feature flag and exercised in staging without regressions
KV checkpoint manifest spec published and checked into docs/confluence
Scheduler reconciler can apply checkpoints on shard warmup without blocking allocation for >50ms
Perf: p95 latency for 512-token sequences does not increase by more than 5% in canary
Automated tests (unit + integration) cover checkpoint read/write and corrupt-manifest recovery
comments: 2026-01-20 - Aisha: Spike complete. Rust FFI approach looks viable; memory-safety wins are promising. PR with minimal shim prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289

2026-01-28 - Jonas: Implemented manifest schema v1. Added fields: shard_id, epoch, last_seq, tombstone_count, checksum (crc32). Shared the draft spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CKPT-Adapter-Spec

2026-02-02 - Eng review (Marta R.): Suggest changing checksum to SHA1 for compatibility with existing tooling. Concern about manifest size for large shards — propose optional chunking header. Action: update spec and add chunking support if size > 4MB.

2026-02-08 - Jonas: Added chunking header and SHA1 checksums. Wrote integration harness that replays checkpoints against a stub kv engine. Found race when reconciler applies checkpoint while prefetch is active; introduced a reconcile barrier to serialize warmup+apply for a shard.

2026-02-14 - QA (Tom): Stress test results attached: staging-canary-2026-02-14.csv (perf dashboard). Noted intermittent 1.2% p95 regression under synthetic burst; attributed to serialization barrier. Follow-up: explore optimistic apply with compare-and-swap on epoch.

2026-02-19 - Security (Priya): Quick review flagged that manifest files may be written to shared NFS in some infra. Recommend signing manifests with HMAC using node key and enabling strict read permissions. Marked ticket with security_review_required=true.

2026-02-20 - Jonas: Implemented HMAC signing for manifests, added KMS integration stub and env var guard. Preparing canary rollout steps and runbook for rollback. Linked canary playbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/playbooks/ckpt-canary.md
